correctness.rationale: The two displayed bounds and their uniform leading-order consequence hold for the coded language. On the right, a terminal zero run of visible length a can be taken complete and extended by ka ones; for a terminal one run of length b, the requisite total one-run length is fixed by a fully observed preceding zero run, or one may choose a zero run of length max(a, ceil(b/k)) if the past is clipped. For an all-one word use ceil(m/k). This costs at most km. On the left, a leading zero run needs only the missing zeros prescribed by a complete first one run (or by the shortest compatible completion of an open first one run); a leading one run of length b needs at most ceil(b/k) zeros and k-1 ones. Joining the two completed junctions proves the upper bound. For t=floor((n-2)/k), the pair 0^(m-1)1 and 01^(kt)0^(n-kt-1) forces disjoint bridge contributions of at least k(m-1)-1 ones and t-1 zeros, since the first block's ones must finish and the later complete kt-run forces exactly t preceding zeros. Their concatenated contribution is admissible, including the empty-bridge case. The coefficients are unequal for k>1 and coincide at 1 for k=1; the prose 'different' is read with this qualification, not as an extra claim for k=1.
